en: Many mistakenly believe Mount Pulag is the tallest, but Mount Apo is actually the highest mountain in the Philippines.
While Taal is famous for recent eruptions, Mayon Volcano is actually the most active volcano in the Philippines.
Many think Mindanao is the largest island, but Luzon is actually the biggest and most populous island in the Philippines.
Despite its name, the Philippine Sea is located on the eastern side of the archipelago, facing the Pacific Ocean.
Many mistakenly group Palawan with the Visayas, but it is officially part of the MIMAROPA region.
Although the Pasig River is historically famous, the Cagayan River is actually the longest river in the Philippines.
People often think Taal Lake is the largest, but Laguna de Bay is actually the biggest lake in the Philippines.
The Philippines is not crossed by the equator, but is located entirely north of it in the Northern Hemisphere.
The Tubbataha Reefs are not attached to Palawan's mainland, but are located in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The Chocolate Hills are not brown all year because their grass turns chocolate brown only during the dry season.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is not a single province, but a region composed of six distinct provinces.
Taal Volcano is not situated on solid mainland, but is uniquely located within Taal Lake in Batangas.
